items.title: Reconcile this backlog with current source and active work
items.problem: Plans and implementation evidence are spread across files; the captured source can change while other tasks work.
scope: Existing roadmap, execution status, open issues and pull requests (read-only)
acceptance: Classify each candidate as implemented, still open, superseded or awaiting evidence; retain source links and reasons.
Inspect dirty state, remotes, worktrees and local environment presence without reading secrets; avoid duplicate work with active owners.
Resolve the actual offline validation commands and record exact current default-branch/working-tree provenance; do not copy historical live passes to newer code.
validation: Read the applicable instructions and validation workflow; read gh issue list and gh pr list for the named repository using nathanmcnulty. Do not create or modify issues/PRs.
evidence: 2026-10-04 read-only reconciliation against current main dee908693cb885e0a04b9a01e9136ec0d84cd0c3: inspected canonical dirty state, remotes, worktrees and environment-path presence without reading values; active/unowned branches remain untouched. Reviewed current issue/PR inventory, roadmap/TODO task sources and .github/workflows/validate.yml; kept live and optional-feature gates proposed.

acceptance: Verify Function and Automation package provenance, manifest failures and exact upstream revision.
For each supported compute/web mode retain job success, hosted asset identity and Easy Auth enforcement evidence.
Document unsupported combinations and teardown; preserve the explicit upstream dependency instead of a false self-contained claim.
validation: After separate authorization, retain redacted exact-target live evidence and cleanup results outside public Git. Do not execute live operations from this backlog alone.

items.title: Evaluate optional WebApp hosting without forking upstream reporting
items.problem: WebApp is a documented future surface; the shared Maester web module has application-specific assumptions.
acceptance: Produce adopt/adapt/defer decision comparing blob-backed Container App with WebApp identity, Easy Auth and asset contracts.
Keep upstream exporter/dashboard source authoritative and compute/web selection independent.
Do not vendor maester-report-webapp unchanged unless its Maester-specific behavior is compatible; define a narrow shared extraction only with two consumers.
evidence: Source-backed optional Web App assessment on 2026-10-10 at published wrapper main 8f258252417cb9f675a8b1ec3a8649582bdca91c. docs/webapp-compatibility-assessment.md compares current Blob-backed Container App identity, Storage Blob reader, asset synchronization and Easy Auth with maester-report-webapp 0.1.1 at immutable Reference revision 29bcc4c8f08855b35f7a357dd2c8c8819824ce7c; the complete component directory is unchanged through inspected Reference main 277584b33fcae7d47113718aad6428abdc4bc50f.

Decision: defer unchanged component adoption. The Maester module serves local wwwroot through pm2 and supplies optional Website Contributor, but does not preserve Defender Blob asset sync/required-file paths, runtime reader assignment or the current tenant/group/auth adapter. The assessment records missing identity, auth, publishing, rollback and ownership contracts rather than treating copied infrastructure as a supported Web App path.

The upstream defender-reporting exporter/dashboard remains authoritative at the existing integrity-bound release; compute and web selection remain independent. No reporting fork, generic shared extraction, component lock, infrastructure, runtime or permission change is introduced. Any later extraction needs equivalent evidence from two real consumers. This completes the original local assessment acceptance without claiming deployed App Service, recipient/browser output or live auth/cleanup qualification.

PowerShell 7.6.6 registered ./scripts/Validate-Repository.ps1 -ValidateAllUpstreamContracts passed parser, private Bicep 0.46.1 compile, upstream Function package build/helper/module staging, Automation runbook build, template publisher contract and hosted asset comparison. Bundled-release Pester 5.7.1 passed 4 tests with zero failures/skips including tampered package/archive rejection. Canonical backlog schema, generated review view and Git whitespace checks passed. No authentication, Azure/Graph mutation or delivery ran.

items.title: Complete the owned PowerShell 7.6 and Pester 6.2 baseline
items.problem: The hosted-runtime draft selected PowerShell 7.6, while owned scripts still declared 7.0 and CI installed Pester 5.7.1.
acceptance: Owned scripts and tests require PowerShell 7.6+ and CI imports exact Pester 6.2.0.
All three workflows that run repository PowerShell explicitly select and verify PowerShell 7.6.6 before repository work.
Preserve locked upstream archives, compatibility contracts, runtime topology and the full contract-validation gate.
validation: Verify vendor archive hashes, unchanged contracts/infra, baseline scan and canonical backlog schema/render checks.
evidence: Source baseline follow-up to draft #21 head dd3a1aa544c9760685ceb20c9e90458ed01b2adb: all fourteen owned scripts and both test files require 7.6; one shared local CI action selects official SHA-256-verified Windows x64 PowerShell 7.6.6 for validation, upstream-update and opt-in smoke workflows. Pester 6.2.0 is explicitly installed/imported and the nonempty suite rejects failed, skipped, inconclusive and unexecuted outcomes. Local PowerShell 7.6.6/.NET 10.0.12 passed 7/7 tests with zero omissions; full locked-upstream gate passed in 22.7 seconds without removing stages. Both ZIPs and all locks/infra remain unchanged. Historical upstream archive requirements are frozen evidence. No live authentication, deployment, export, schedule mutation, grant or workflow dispatch occurred; issue #20 and REPORT-002 retain separate native qualification gates.
